content:
Hey all, I recently built a small agentic Lean 4 prover for a Hugging Face hackathon and wanted to share it here since this is probably the right audience to actually appreciate (or critique) what's going on under the hood.

The setup: a local 27B model hosted on a cloud GPU proposes tactics, the Lean kernel verifies each step, and errors feed back into the next proposal. Nothing novel architecturally, but getting the REPL integration working reliably was the interesting part.

It handles propositional logic and classical reasoning reasonably well. ¬¬P → P gets solved via Classical.byContradiction after a couple of failed attempts, De Morgan, associativity, etc. It visibly struggles with induction over List functions where you need omega after unfolding, it keeps throwing more simp lemmas at it instead of switching strategy.

It's far from perfect, but if you want to poke at it the Space is free to use. Would love to hear how it handles theorems I haven't tested yet, especially from people who know Lean better than I do.

https://huggingface.co/spaces/build-small-hackathon/QED

Curious if anyone has thoughts on the omega after induction gap specifically, is that a tactic ordering problem or a prompt engineering problem?
